title: Seeing Past the Cataract

patient.name: Mdm Lee Bee Choo
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for Potential Acuity Meter (PAM) before cataract surgery — dense cataract in the right eye

history.hpc: Mdm Lee says 'My right eye very blur now, like looking through frosted glass.' The doctor found a dense cataract and ordered a PAM test to estimate how well she might see after surgery, since the dense lens makes it hard to assess the retina.
history.pmhx: Dense right cataract. No diabetes. No known macular disease.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Dense nuclear cataract in the right eye limiting the fundus view
examination_findings.fundus: Right fundus view obscured by the cataract

pam.device: Potential Acuity Meter (projects a chart onto the retina, bypassing the cataract)
pam.preparation: Pupil dilated as required for PAM
pam.interpretation: Despite the dense cataract, the retina appears to have good potential, suggesting a good visual outcome after surgery

diagnosis: PAM completed on the right eye after dilation, projecting a chart through the dense cataract. Predicted potential acuity is good (around 6/9), suggesting the retina is healthy and a good visual outcome is likely after cataract surgery. The result is reported to the surgeon; the OT does not make the surgical decision.

immediate: Confirm identity and confirm the eye to be tested against the order
Confirm the pupil is adequately dilated (required for PAM)
Explain the test: looks into a machine and reads a chart projected into the eye, quick and painless
Set up the PAM and position the patient at the chinrest
Obtain the best predicted acuity, repeating to confirm consistency
Record the predicted acuity and provide the result to the doctor
follow_up: Surgeon to use the PAM result when counselling the patient on expected outcome
Correlate with fundus assessment once the cataract is removed
patient_education: Explain the test estimates how well she may see after the cataract is removed
Reassure the test is quick and painless
Explain dilation will blur near vision for a few hours

key_points: Confirms identity and the correct eye to test
Confirms the pupil is dilated as required for PAM
Explains the purpose and nature of the test
Checks the order from the doctor
Sets up the PAM correctly and positions the patient
Repeats to confirm a consistent result
Understands PAM predicts vision behind a cataract
Recognises a good predicted acuity suggests a good outcome
Does not make the surgical decision — reports to the doctor
Knows dilation is required for the test
Provides the result to the surgeon
Documents the predicted acuity and the eye
Educates the patient on the test and dilation effects
